instruction_text: Warm, bright, cozy storytelling in the manner of a well-loved radio feature: unhurried, richly expressive, with full vowels and gentle emphasis, never flat or sleepy. Let the pitch rise and fall a little more on key words. Add a touch more brightness and a hint of a smile in the voice, while staying unhurried. Articulate crisply: distinct consonants, clean word endings, every syllable clearly heard.
asr_text: Coffee prices are falling. Great. Maybe spring will finally come to my wallet, too. But supermarket prices do not change. They look calm, as if saying, news? I haven't heard any. If bean prices have fallen, why don't we pay less? First, let's go back to when high prices caused a stir. Bad weather in Brazil and Vietnam hurt the supply. Few beans were for sale, and stocks were low. Then demand around the world was strong. It was a hard mix for prices to settle down. At about the same time, ICE's future prices for Arabica coffee reached a record high. But future prices are not prices for green beans sold right away. They are not store prices either. They may all wear the same name tag, coffee price, but they mean different things.
